thesis_triggers.event: At ~$40 the market would price Centrus near its horizon cash floor ($26.67: net cash after the build spend, Westerman, run-off core, less OPEB) plus part of the DOE-funded HALEU leg, i.e. as if the LEU build had failed, been cut back or needed financing at distressed terms; likeliest triggers: a capex figure far above ~$1,350/SWU-yr at the December Investor Day, a denied TENEX waiver plus a forced raise, or loss of DOE milestone funding.

supervisor_summary: Centrus is a finite Russian/Orano SWU resale book plus net cash funding an undisclosed-cost, first-of-a-kind Piketon enrichment build; the reconciled research value is $45 at the horizon versus $109.88 today, because at ~$1,350/SWU-yr and ~$200-230/SWU the initial cascades barely earn their cost and value rests on net cash, the DOE-funded HALEU leg and options. Round 2 added OPEB (-$2.3/share), a tax build (+$3/share) and fixed warrant cash in the bull state; Orano-like capex would lift the value to $60. The December Piketon Investor Day (announced on the Q2 call, which I missed in round 1) is the likeliest first capex disclosure and the event that decides who is right. The five ladders agree closely, so the ladder stays at their mean (P(>= $110) ~0.32); thesis break $40; size small (89% realised volatility, ~30% short interest, lock-up ends ~11-08, TENEX waiver pending).
key_drivers: Build-out cost per SWU-yr and capacity are undisclosed ('multi-billion'): at Orano-like cost (-35% post-horizon capex) the research value is $59.92 vs $45.35; the December 2026 Piketon Investor Day (Q2 call) is the likely first disclosure.

The trading book is finite: 'well over one-half' of LEU deliveries through 2027 come from TENEX, the third (2026-27) waiver application is still pending and no waivers exist after 2027, so FY2028 core EBIT falls to a small run-off (10-Q, 10-K).

Cash, not earnings, carries value: ~$1.06B pro forma net cash today falls to ~$550M at the horizon incl. an expected raise; OPEB $71.7M, $1.2B converts at face and 6.99M warrants ($227-363) sit ahead of common holders.
The DOE $900M HALEU task order (~40% in 2028, ~30% on completion of the initial phase in 2031) is the most bankable piece (PV ~$640M risked, ~$506M after tax).
At $109.88 the market prices the build at ~$1.3B net of spend, roughly the bull state; sell-side targets ($230 average, Needham cut to $206 on 10-20) sit far above any driver build.
